before_taxonomy.classification_basis: Human scammers used deepfake executives in a live video call to supply false senior payment authority. The finance director then transferred more than US$499,000. The AI-mediated economic deception and the use of fabricated executive identity to steer that human decision are distinct supported aspects of the scheme. Police withholding and seizure of funds are later response actions; the release does not establish when funds were returned to the company.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Human scammers used deepfake representations of senior company personnel in a live video conference to create materially false executive payment authority and induce a transfer exceeding US$499,000. The deceptive economic framing was materially AI-mediated while the scam objective remained human-directed.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: Deepfake executives in a Zoom meeting supplied false senior authority to the finance director, who transferred more than US$499,000.

classification_review_provenance.review_status: Evidence-first HIM and relational/protection fidelity review; prior roles accounted for.

after_taxonomy.classification_basis: Human scammers used deepfake executives in a live video call to supply false senior payment authority. The finance director then transferred more than US$499,000. clauses.source_paraphrase: On 24 March 2025, a WhatsApp sender impersonating the company’s chief financial officer arranged a restructuring discussion. A purported lawyer stressed confidentiality and obtained a non-disclosure agreement.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The initial contact and confidentiality framing precede the AI-mediated executive impersonation.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 25 March, the finance director joined a rescheduled Zoom call with deepfake executive impersonators. That call and later messages from the purported lawyer supplied instructions for the payment made the following day.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Synthetic executive presence and coordinated human messages can provide false authority for an economic decision.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The synthetic executives supplied the materially false corporate authority context on which the victim relied when transferring funds, while police evidence later supported recovery.
Deepfake executives in a Zoom meeting supplied false senior authority to the finance director, who transferred more than US$499,000.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 26 March, the director transferred more than US$499,000 to a local corporate mule account. More than US$494,000 then went to Hong Kong accounts.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: An executed transfer and subsequent fund movement are distinct from the preceding solicitation.

clauses.source_paraphrase: A further request for US$1.4 million on 27 March prompted discovery. The director alerted HSBC, which notified Singapore’s Anti-Scam Centre.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Detection and escalation occurred after the first transfer; the additional requested amount is not another realised loss.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 28 March, Hong Kong police withheld the amount transferred there, and Singapore police seized more than US$5,000 remaining locally. The police release described an ongoing investigation.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Withholding and seizure mitigate loss but do not establish the date funds were returned to the victim.

notes: Police seizure/withholding is not a dated return of funds. The call and payment chronology are distinct. No identified source-image consent facts are invented for an additional identity-synthesis mapping.
